01Servicing and optimisation of an existing domestic treatment plant

Servicing and optimisation of an existing domestic treatment plant

The owners of a holiday property came to us with a long-standing problem with their ASIO VARIOcomp 5K domestic wastewater treatment plant.

Ever since the plant was put into operation, they had struggled above all with a strong odour, noticeable not only around the property but also inside the cottage. Running the plant had therefore long been very unpleasant for the family.

02First we had to find the real cause

First we had to find the real cause

During the initial technical inspection we found that the plant's technology itself had not been connected correctly and that the original installation had several shortcomings.

These were mainly incorrect process connections between the individual parts of the plant and poorly executed hose and electrical runs, which among other things lacked proper protective conduits.

So simply changing the control unit settings or adding bacteria was not enough. First we had to remove the causes that were preventing the technology and the biological process from working properly.

03Modifying the technology and stabilising the biological process

Modifying the technology and stabilising the biological process

After assessing the situation, we made the necessary changes to the process connections and the installation.

To support the biological process and help it stabilise faster, we then added microbial sludge and a biological carrier, and began controlled dosing of nutrients for the microorganisms.

The results began to show within just a few days.

The biological process gradually stabilised, the activated sludge began to settle very well, and clean treated water was clearly visible at the plant's outlet.

04Once the biology had become successfully established, we stopped dosing nutrients and monitored further progress using…

Once the biology had become successfully established, we stopped dosing nutrients and monitored further progress using sedimentation tests. These confirmed that good-quality, well-settling activated sludge was forming.

05And the original odour problem?

And the original odour problem?

Gone.

Once the installation faults had been put right and the biological process stabilised, the plant stopped causing odour problems both around and inside the property.

The family can finally use the treatment plant the way they expected to from the very beginning.

06We don't just fix the fault. We assess the WWTP as a whole.

We don't just fix the fault. We assess the WWTP as a whole.

During a service visit we don't focus solely on fixing the fault at hand.

We can carry out an independent technical and process assessment of an existing domestic WWTP, whoever its manufacturer, and evaluate whether its design, size, connections and operating settings match the way the property is actually used.

We assess, for example:

  • the condition and function of the individual process components,
  • whether the process connections are correct,
  • the hydraulic load on the plant and any fluctuations in it,
  • the pollutant and biological load,
  • the condition and settling properties of the activated sludge,
  • the aeration settings and the individual operating cycles,
  • the quality of the effluent,
  • possible causes of odour or unstable operation.
07If we find that the existing solution does not match the actual conditions, we can then prepare a proposal…

If we find that the existing solution does not match the actual conditions, we can then prepare a proposal for specific corrective measures – from changing the operating settings and modifying the technology to extending or modernising it.

Our aim is not to recommend replacing the whole plant as a matter of course. If the problem can be solved by correct settings or a suitable modification of the existing technology, that is the route we look for first.

08Prevention is easier than solving problems

Prevention is easier than solving problems

A domestic WWTP is a biological technology whose operation can change with the number of occupants, the volume and nature of the incoming wastewater and the way the property is used.

We therefore recommend having the plant checked at least twice a year by an experienced service technician or process engineer.

Regular checks make it possible to assess the condition of the technology and the biological process in good time and to deal with any problems before they show up as odour, poorer sludge settling or lower quality of the treated water.

09Čistá řešení – it's not enough for a treatment plant just to run.

Čistá řešení – it's not enough for a treatment plant just to run. What matters is that it treats the water properly.
